title: Been building a Greek myth ARPG on my own since September. Here's where Act I is at.
author: Olympus_TCG
selftext:
This is Olympus: The Corrupted Gods. You wash up on the Greek coast after a shipwreck and find the gods corrupted by Atë, the goddess of ruin, and it's on you to stop her. Four classes so far: Hoplite, Toxotes (archer), Sibyl and Psychopomp. The clip is all Act I, plus two of its bosses, Glaukos and the Polemarch.

Being upfront because people always ask: I use AI a lot. Claude writes most of the code, the 3D models come from Tripo, and the music and voices are ElevenLabs. I make the calls on what goes in and what gets thrown out, and I throw out a lot. It's built in Godot 4.

The characters in the video are high-level test builds with the tree filled in, so the skills are fully kitted. A normal character won't clear packs this fast at the start. The audio is just one of the game's music tracks.

Plenty is still rough. The animations need the most work and I'm on them now. Path of Exile 2 is the obvious inspiration, especially for combat and how the zones are laid out.

Plan is an Act I demo on Steam sometime in 2027. What I'd really like to know: does the combat read clearly? Can you tell what's happening in the big fights?

replies.author: Olympus_TCG
replies.body:
I actually use both. the older hero models and the first enemies were meshy, most of the props and the newer creatures are tripo. 

what made tripo work for me was never using text to 3d. I make a concept image first, run multiview on it, look at all 4 views and delete any that are wrong, then do multiview to 3d. 

settings are H3.1, ultra mesh, 4k textures, remove lighting on.

the raw download never goes in the game as is though. everything goes through a blender script that scales it to real size, cuts the polycount, bakes AO and packs each set of props onto one texture. that cleanup is probably half of why it looks ok

comments.author: Maksim_Volganin_11
comments.body:
For a solo project built since September, this is seriously impressive—the UI, the constellation skill tree, and the overall PoE2/Titan Quest vibe already look great.
To answer your question honestly about combat readability: 
it’s pretty clear in the 1v1 boss fights (like Glaukos), but gets quite chaotic in large packs (especially around 0:20–0:23 and 0:30).
A couple of things that stood out:
Character silhouette gets lost: In dense crowds, the player character blends into the enemies and ground textures. A subtle rim light, a slightly brighter palette for the player, or a faint ground ring could help keep track of your position instantly.
VFX vs. enemy telegraphs: The lightning bursts and white flashes look cool, but they completely cover enemy wind-up animations. Toning down the opacity/bloom of player AoE effects slightly will make incoming hits much easier to read.
Damage numbers: Making them slightly smaller or having them fade faster would free up a lot of screen space during heavy AoE.
Really cool progress though—curating AI assets into a cohesive look is way harder than people think, and you're pulling it off well.
